goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — String#scrub does not exist on any Ruby version this codebase supports

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). `String#scrub` is not available in older Ruby versions (notably Ruby 1.9/2.0). The repo’s Gemfile comment about tools “only works on 1.9” suggests the codebase may run on pre-2.1 Rubies, in which case this call would raise `NoMethodError` at runtime when polling feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed HTML is rendered unsanitized as raw HTML (CGI.unescapeHTML passed to TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html, rendered via `raw post.cooked`), enabling stored XSS from feed content in poll_feed.rb:31-33

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` (poll_feed.rb:31-38). `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)` (topic_embed.rb:20-33). `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html` (post.rb:124-132), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (embed/best.html.erb:17). There is no sanitization step for feed-provided HTML, so malicious HTML/JS from the feed can be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: imported_from footer in topic_embed.rb:15 interpolates the raw feed URL into a single-quoted href without escaping, allowing HTML/attribute injection via crafted URLs that pass the regex check

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet containing `#{url}` (raw interpolation into a single-quoted attribute) after only validating `url` with `^https?\:\/\/` (start-with check). A crafted URL like `http://example.com' onmouseover='...` would pass the regex and break out of the `href` attribute, enabling HTML/attribute injection. This is especially impactful because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (no sanitization), and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 crashes with NoMethodError when i.content is nil for standard RSS 2.0 feeds (which use description, not content), with no fallback to i.description and no rescue, silently killing all importing
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling methods on `i.content` assumes it is always present, but many RSS feeds only provide `description`, so `i.content` can be nil and cause a NoMethodError/nil exception; both recommend/mention needing a fallback to `i.description` to avoid crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation asymmetry between embed_controller.rb (checks only referer host) and topic_retriever.rb (also requires embed_url host to match embeddable_host) causes a permanent infinite 30-second reload loop with no terminal error state for legitimate embeds whose URL points at a different host

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated only by `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the `embed_url` param itself is not validated there. When no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, the controller enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`, whose view forces a `document.location.reload()` every 30s. In `TopicRetriever`, `retrieve` will skip `perform_retrieve` if `invalid_host?` is true, where `invalid_host?` requires `URI(@embed_url).host` to exactly equal `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Therefore if the request referer host matches `embeddable_host` but the `embed_url` host differs (e.g., www vs non-www), retrieval will never happen and the embed endpoint will keep returning the loading page, producing an infinite reload loop with no terminal error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability path) has no test coverage; topic_embed_spec.rb only covers .import

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, which fetches remote content via `open(url).read` and parses it with `Readability::Document` before delegating to `TopicEmbed.import`. The added specs (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) cover only `.import` (creation/update and URL absolutization) and do not exercise the `import_remote` Readability/HTTP-fetch path. No other new spec file covers `import_remote`, so the new nontrivial logic is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) calls in poll_feed.rb:30 and topic_embed.rb:41 lack read_timeout/error handling, allowing a hung remote host to block the Sidekiq worker indefinitely and stall scheduled polling

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote network fetches inside Sidekiq jobs without any explicit timeout or exception handling: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`. These run in scheduled/async workers (`PollFeed` hourly, `RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever`) and, as written, can block a worker for an unbounded/long time or crash the job on transient network errors, disrupting polling/retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile.lock for the standard bundle is not updated in the diff (only Gemfile_rails4.lock), leaving the primary lockfile stale and breaking bundle install --frozen/--deployment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new gems in `Gemfile` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but it does not show any corresponding update to a standard `Gemfile.lock`. From the diff alone we can verify only that the Rails 4 lockfile was updated; whether there is a primary `Gemfile.lock` in the repo and whether deployment uses it (and would break with `--frozen/--deployment`) is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:5-11 lacks a null check on #discourse-comments before appendChild, throwing a TypeError and rendering nothing when the div is missing, with no diagnosable failure

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code assigns `comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError, preventing the embed from rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed.js snippet ships with no documentation explaining the required #discourse-comments div, which is the only coupling point between the snippet and the page

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the snippet hard-codes `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally does `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. The diff does not include any inline comment or external documentation describing the required `#discourse-comments` container on the embedding page, so the reviewer’s point about missing documentation for this coupling is diff-grounded (even though it’s not a functional defect by itself).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR title claims 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation system' but the diff ships an entire new embedding subsystem (gem dependencies, new tables, cook_method schema change, poll_feed job, new site settings, public route, Disqus task rewrite) — scope drift; block until intent is restated or diff is split

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a broad new embedding/importing subsystem: adds new gem deps (ruby-readability, simple-rss), new controller/view/layout/assets for embeds, new public route `get 'embed/best'`, new models/migrations (`topic_embeds` table, `posts.cook_method`), new jobs (`RetrieveTopic`, scheduled `PollFeed`), new site settings under `embedding`, and rewrites the Disqus import task to use `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. That is a substantial feature set beyond “URL handling/validation” alone, so the scope/PR-splitting concern is diff-grounded. However, the specific mismatch vs the PR title itself can’t be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 adds force: true to an already-shipped migration with no connection to embedding — re-running it will silently DROP and recreate top_topics, destroying all accumulated ranking data

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which would drop and recreate `top_topics` if that migration is executed while the table already exists. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify the premise that this will run against an already-migrated production DB (Rails won’t re-run applied migrations), so the described data-loss scenario is conditional. It’s still a concrete, diff-grounded concern because modifying an old migration and adding `force: true` increases risk in nonstandard flows (e.g., running this migration on a DB where `top_topics` already exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-141 silently removes the documented --category option and replaces PostCreator-based import with TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking existing scripted invocations passing -c (Thor raises on unknown options) and turning imports into a live HTTP fetch per thread with no stated requirement

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed and the corresponding `options[:category]` handling and `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` call are deleted. The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs `open(url).read` (live HTTP fetch) via ruby-readability. This is a behavior/CLI-compatibility regression: existing scripted invocations that pass `-c/--category` will no longer be accepted (Thor typically errors on unknown options), and imports now depend on remote HTTP instead of using the provided Disqus thread data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 calls i.content.scrub assuming all feed items have a <content> element; SimpleRSS only defines accessors for present elements, so feeds with <description>/<summary> cause NoMethodError, aborting poll_feed mid-iteration and silently skipping the remaining items every hour

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., only has description/summary), `i.content` can be nil, making `.scrub` raise NoMethodError and abort the job mid-iteration. The diff shows no nil-guard or fallback to other fields, so this is a real failure mode introduced by the new feed-import logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 use open(url) with no read_timeout, redirect, or size limits and slurp the entire body into memory — a stalled feed_polling_url ties up a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and a malicious embed_url can return an unbounded body and exhaust worker memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded network reads in Sidekiq jobs: `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`. Neither specifies timeouts, redirect limits, or response-size limits, and `import_remote` explicitly slurps the full body into memory. A slow/stalled URL can tie up a Sidekiq worker, and a large/malicious response can exhaust memory—this is a real availability/security defect grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:353-356 plus client.en.yml:1477 add the embedding settings group label but no admin template/route, leaving embeddable_host, feed_polling_enabled, feed_polling_url, and embed_by_username unsettable from the admin panel so the feature cannot be enabled without console access

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `embedding:` category to `config/site_settings.yml` and also adds the corresponding admin UI category label `embedding: "Embedding"` under `js.admin.site_settings.categories` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`. In Discourse, site settings categories are driven by `site_settings.yml` + these translations, so the presence of both strongly indicates these settings will be shown in the existing admin settings UI without needing a new route/template. The finding’s claim that the settings are “unsettable from the admin panel” is not supported by what’s shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb contains whitespace-only churn (trailing-space removal, newline deletion at EOF) that pollutes git blame and couples unrelated migration changes to any future revert of the embed feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff to db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb is purely whitespace/formatting (removing a trailing-space-only line after disable_ddl_transaction! and changing the EOF newline, as indicated by “No newline at end of file”). This does not introduce a functional defect; it’s a style/format nit about blame/churn rather than a correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14 self.import mutates the caller's contents string in place (contents << "\n<hr>..."), so a future caller reusing its content buffer (e.g., in-memory retry) would repeatedly append the 'Imported from' footer and change the sha1, triggering spurious revisions

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller-provided String in place before computing `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. If the same `contents` String object is reused across calls (or even within a retry loop), the footer will be appended repeatedly, changing the SHA1 and causing unnecessary revisions. The in-place mutation is directly present in the diff and can produce incorrect behavior in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:4 has an unused require_dependency 'email/sender' — dead copy-paste code that misleads readers into looking for an email path in this job

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb the job declares `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the code in this diff only uses `TopicRetriever` (and `User`), with no references to `Email::Sender` or related email functionality. That makes the require appear unnecessary/copy-pasted, adding misleading coupling and avoidable load work, though it doesn't change runtime behavior in an obvious way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting an imported topic orphans the topic_embeds row (no FK, no dependent: cleanup), so topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead topic id, best raises NotFound, and the retrieve_topic fallback never fires — the URL can never re-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed` with `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` but no `dependent: :destroy` hooks anywhere, and the migration `create_topic_embeds` adds no foreign keys—only a unique index on `embed_url`. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns the stored `topic_id` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) without checking the topic still exists. In `EmbedController#best`, any non-nil `topic_id` skips the re-import enqueue path and calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, which will fail if that topic was deleted, preventing the intended fallback (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`) from ever running for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 calls i.content.scrub which raises NoMethodError on feed items without a content element (nil from SimpleRSS); with retry: false the scheduled run aborts mid-each, silently skipping all subsequent items every hour

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil for a given SimpleRSS item (e.g., feeds that only provide `description`/`summary`/`content_encoded`), `nil.scrub` will raise NoMethodError and abort the job partway through `rss.items.each`. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried and the remaining items in that run won’t be processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is computed over contents after appending the locale-dependent 'imported from' footer (input mutated in place), so translation/locale changes cause mass spurious revisions of all imported posts; sha1 should be computed before appending the footer

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code mutates `contents` by appending the locale-dependent footer (`contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)}..."`) *before* computing `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. Because the footer text comes from I18n (`embed.imported_from`), changes in locale/translation will change the SHA1 and make previously-imported posts appear “updated”, triggering unnecessary revisions (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 ... revisor.revise! ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The no-topic embed path has no terminal failure state: controller enqueues retrieve_topic before TopicRetriever's 60s setnx throttle, so permanently unfetchable URLs cause every visitor to enqueue a Sidekiq job every 30s indefinitely, flooding the queue

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so if an embed is never created (e.g., fetch/import fails), each reload/request will enqueue another Sidekiq job indefinitely. The 60s Redis throttle is only applied inside TopicRetriever#retrieve (lib/topic_retriever.rb) which runs in the job, so it reduces work but does not prevent queue growth/enqueue storms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is matched by exact string equality with no canonicalization, so trailing slash/scheme/query differences between the feed link and discourseEmbedUrl create duplicate topics for the same article; normalization should happen at the single import entry point

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact string value of the URL (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` in `topic_id_for_embed`) with only a basic `^https?://` check and no normalization/canonicalization. Since the unique index is only on the raw `embed_url` string, URL variants (scheme, trailing slash, query params, etc.) will be treated as different and can create separate topics/embeds for the same article when coming from different sources (feed `i.link`/`i.id` vs. `discourseEmbedUrl` param).

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key ('feed-modified:#{sha1}') is dead code with no read, write, or expiry anywhere — either delete it or implement the conditional-poll/etag design it scaffolds

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to memoize a Redis/cache key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`), but it is never referenced anywhere in `execute` or `poll_feed`, nor anywhere else in the provided diff. Since there’s no read/write/expiry usage tied to this key, it’s effectively dead scaffolding and should either be removed or completed with conditional polling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), inlining a full scheduled feed poll into the retrieval path and bypassing scheduler/recurrence semantics; extract a shared import helper or pass the URL instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` directly calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed` is defined as a scheduled job (`class PollFeed < Jobs::Scheduled`, `recurrence { hourly }`), but this invocation runs it inline on the embed retrieval path, potentially polling/importing the entire configured feed synchronously just to satisfy a single `@embed_url` lookup. This is a concrete design/performance/semantics concern grounded in the code, not a provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Both open(...) calls (poll_feed.rb:30, topic_embed.rb:52) lack timeouts, so a hung feed host or article server wedges a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and starves the queue

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without any timeout controls: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`. With `open-uri`, lack of `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` means these calls can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely if the remote host hangs, effectively starving the queue. This is a real reliability defect introduced by the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds.topic_id/post_id have no FK or invariant enforcing post.topic_id == topic_id, so future writers (e.g. admin post moves) can split them undetected; the model has no on_delete story

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with separate `topic_id` and `post_id` columns (`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`) and the model declares `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` but adds no validation tying them together (e.g., ensuring `post.topic_id == topic_id`) and no FK constraints or `dependent:` behavior. This can allow silent inconsistency/orphans if posts/topics are later moved/deleted by other code paths. The diff does not show an immediate runtime failure, but it is a real integrity/maintenance concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR-level objective drift: the stated objective (embed URL handling/validation) does not cover the new RSS/Atom feed import feature (PollFeed scheduled job, ruby-readability/simple-rss gems, three new site settings), rewritten Disqus importer, global PostRevisor validation loosening, and global Post#cook change — all shipped without explicit acceptance of the new scope

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly expands scope well beyond embed URL handling/validation: it adds RSS/Atom feed importing via a new scheduled job (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) and new dependencies (Gemfile: ruby-readability, simple-rss; lockfile additions), introduces three new site settings under `embedding` (config/site_settings.yml + server locale strings), rewrites the Disqus importer to call TopicEmbed.import_remote (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), loosens validation on post revisions globally when `skip_validations` is passed (@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) in lib/post_revisor.rb), and changes Post#cook behavior globally to allow `raw_html` bypass (app/models/post.rb) with a new DB column/migration. That’s a concrete PR-level scope/acceptance concern grounded in the changes, not a directly verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117-152: Disqus importer contract silently repurposed — category option, category_id lookup, and permalink placeholder post removed; existing automation passing '-c Category' loses category placement or errors, and first posts now contain Readability-scraped HTML from the live URL instead of local permalink stubs, breaking offline/partial Disqus exports

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `:category` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor: `method_option :category` deleted) and the associated `category_id` lookup + `PostCreator` call that used it. Any existing automation invoking `disqus:import -c ...` will now fail with an unknown option (or at minimum lose category placement), which is a concrete backwards-incompatible behavior change introduced by this diff. The initial post creation also changes from a local permalink stub (`raw: "[[Permalink](...)]"`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which fetches live HTML via Readability/open(url), so offline/partial exports plausibly break under the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4: 'force: true' added to an existing previously-shipped migration — on environments with a pending migration but existing top_topics table, the table will be silently dropped and recreated, destroying existing rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. So if an environment has this migration still pending but already has a `top_topics` table (e.g., created earlier by a different branch/manual change), running the migration would silently drop and recreate the table, losing existing rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:1-33: trailing-whitespace and final-newline-only edits to an unrelated historical migration add diff noise with no semantic change

adjudication.rationale: The referenced migration diff only removes trailing whitespace after `disable_ddl_transaction!` and adds a missing final newline at EOF. This is purely formatting/diff-noise with no semantic or behavioral change, so it’s a style nit rather than a substantive review issue under the given categories.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131-136: new 'cook_method == raw_html → return raw' branch permanently redefines Post#cook contract, dropping the guarantee that cooked content passes the sanitization/cooking pipeline; no model-layer invariant restricts raw_html to feed imports, and after_post_cook plugin filters stop applying to such posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Post#cook to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization path (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The new cook_method can be set via PostCreator options (lib/post_creator.rb) and posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` for RSS/import (TopicEmbed.import) without any model-level restriction shown. PollFeed imports `i.content` directly into raw_html posts (jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so untrusted feed HTML could be rendered as-is, making this a verifiable security/correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19-21: 'feed_key' is dead code — the 'feed-modified:' SHA1 key is defined but never written or read, evidence of an abandoned change-tracking requirement; next maintainer may assume modified-tracking exists

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` (lines ~19-21) computes and memoizes a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere else in the diff: `execute` only calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` unconditionally parses the feed and iterates `rss.items` without reading/writing any modified/etag timestamp. So the finding that `feed_key` is dead/unused code is verifiable from the diff and represents a maintainability/incompleteness concern rather than an immediately broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: feed content imported with zero sanitization and cooked via raw_html method, rendered raw in embed/best.html.erb, allowing script/iframe injection from poisoned feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a raw HTML cooking path and uses it for feed/imported content without any sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `i.content` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` (after only `CGI.unescapeHTML`), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, raw_html returns `raw` (skipping the rendering/sanitization pipeline), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination allows arbitrary HTML/JS from a poisoned feed/article to be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS (e.g., `<script>`/`<iframe>` injection).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: TopicEmbed interpolates unescaped URL into single-quoted HTML attribute in imported_from footer; URL only validated against a basic regex, enabling attribute breakout injection

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` (single-quoted HTML attribute) and later creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` without sanitization. The only URL check is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which would allow a URL containing a single quote and extra attributes (e.g., `http://x.com' onmouseover='...`) to pass, breaking out of the `href` attribute and resulting in stored XSS. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making the injection reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF: host check validates only the initial embed_url; open(url) follows redirects without re-validating host, allowing redirect to internal targets like metadata endpoints or localhost

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: TopicRetriever#invalid_host? only checks the host of the initially supplied @embed_url (URI(@embed_url).host) against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but then fetch_http calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url), which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) without any redirect/endpoint re-validation. Since open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, an allowed external URL on the embeddable_host can redirect to a different host (including internal/localhost/metadata IPs), enabling SSRF beyond the initial host check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed controller access gate relies solely on client-supplied Referer header with no auth or rate limiting, allowing unauthenticated remote trigger of the server-side fetch pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbedController#best is publicly reachable (route `get 'embed/best'`) and, when no TopicEmbed exists, enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` with no authentication requirement (`current_user` may be nil). The only access gate in `ensure_embeddable` is `URI(request.referer||'').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which depends on the client-supplied Referer header and is spoofable. Although `TopicRetriever` adds a per-URL 60s throttle and checks the embed_url host against `embeddable_host`, an unauthenticated attacker can still trigger server-side fetch attempts (and job enqueueing) by forging Referer and varying embed_url paths on the allowed host, so the core security concern is verifiable in the diff (the finding’s “no rate limiting” part is overstated, but does not negate the defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Kernel#open (not URI.open) used in import_remote before any scheme validation; disqus.thor call site passes third-party export links with no host/scheme check, enabling command execution via leading pipe

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code calls `open(url).read` with no scheme/format validation (and without using `URI.open`). Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats strings beginning with `|` as a command (via `IO.popen`), enabling command execution if an attacker can influence `url`. The `disqus.thor` change now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` where `t[:link]` comes from a third-party export and is not host/scheme-checked in this diff, so the risk is exposed at that call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle keyed only on attacker-chosen URL, not per-IP/requestor; unique URLs bypass it, enabling Redis key exhaustion and Sidekiq queue flooding as an outbound-request amplifier

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` the throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (no IP/user component) with a 60s TTL, so an attacker can bypass throttling by varying `embed_url`. Worse, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for every miss (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)`), so unique URLs will both flood Sidekiq and cause many Redis keys to be created. Since `perform_retrieve` ultimately does `open(url).read` via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, this also enables outbound-request amplification to arbitrary paths on the configured `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls and readability allowlist do not filter URI schemes, allowing javascript: URIs in href attributes to survive import and trigger stored XSS on click

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, Readability is configured to allow `a` tags with `href` (`attributes: %w[href src]`) and the resulting `doc.content` is imported as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, raw_html posts return `raw` and skip the normal cooking/rendering pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs starting with `/` and does not validate/filter URI schemes, so an imported `<a href="javascript:...">` would survive and be stored/rendered, enabling stored XSS on click.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12–30 — the three 'requires...' guard tests are false-confidence: each stubs only one setting while others keep real defaults, so execute short-circuits before the condition under test is evaluated; deleting any one of the three guards from the && chain leaves all three tests green

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute the guard is a single `if` with `&&` short-circuiting (`feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`). In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples only stub the one setting under test, but do not stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the defaults in config/site_settings.yml (`feed_polling_enabled: false`, blank strings for the others), the condition will already fail on the first term, so those tests can pass without ever exercising the later terms. Thus they provide false confidence as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:36–43 — 'tells the topic retriever to work' stubs TopicRetriever at the wrong layer and matches any arguments, so the test passes whether or not Jobs.enqueue receives :retrieve_topic with correct user_id and embed_url; the controller's actual contract (enqueueing the right job with the right args) is never asserted

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and never instantiates `TopicRetriever`. However, the spec at `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, and does not assert that `Jobs.enqueue` is called with the correct job name/args. This is a diff-grounded testing/contract issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:28–41 — ADVISORY: the two 'valid host' tests are mirror-tests that stub away all real logic (retrieved_recently? redis throttle and perform_retrieve with dedup check, inline job dispatch, and fetch_http user-lookup), so the throttle can regress (e.g., expire call dropped, making the key live forever) and every test still passes

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the two “valid host” examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to `false`/`true` and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. This means none of the real throttle logic in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire` behavior) is exercised, and none of `perform_retrieve`’s real behavior (dedup via `TopicEmbed.exists?`, optional `Jobs::PollFeed` execution, and `fetch_http` user lookup / import) is tested. As the finding notes, a regression inside those methods (e.g., dropping the `expire` call so the key never expires) would not fail these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41–44 — ADVISORY: 'Supports updating the post' never asserts embed.content_sha1 was updated nor that an identical re-import is a no-op; the test passes even if the sha1-change gate were inverted, removed, or update_column deleted, so every-poll rewrites would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the "Supports updating the post" example only checks that post.cooked changes after calling TopicEmbed.import with new contents. It never asserts that the associated TopicEmbed record’s content_sha1 is updated (embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)) nor that re-importing identical contents becomes a no-op (the content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 guard). Therefore a regression where content_sha1 is not persisted (or where imports always rewrite on every poll) would not be caught by this test, even though that behavior is part of the new logic introduced in TopicEmbed.import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:46–48 — ADVISORY: 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' is a pure constructor-args spy on TopicView.new; nothing checks that best: 5 actually constrains @topic_view.posts or that the template renders correctly, so rendering zero or every post stays green

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best` which instantiates `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. The spec `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` only asserts that `TopicView.new` is called with `{best: 5}` (a constructor-args expectation) and does not exercise the actual rendered output (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) or verify that the `best: 5` option results in `@topic_view.posts` being constrained to highlights/5 posts. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration add_cook_method_to_posts uses default: 1 which maps to raw_html instead of regular (0), silently reclassifying every existing and new post as raw_html

adjudication.rationale: The migration sets `cook_method` default to `1` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). In the same diff, imported RSS/remote content explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating the post (TopicEmbed.import), which implies `:raw_html` is *not* the default value. If `:raw_html` were `1`, this explicit setting would be redundant. So the finding’s claim that `default: 1` maps to `raw_html` and would silently reclassify posts is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfilled and new posts with cook_method=1 cause Post#cook to return raw markdown instead of cooked HTML, so editing any post re-renders cooked content as unprocessed markdown

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Post#cook` only returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`; otherwise it runs the normal cooking pipeline via `post_analyzer.cook(*args)`. The migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`, and the new enum is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which (consistent with existing `Post.types` usage where default `1` maps to `:regular`) means `cook_method=1` is the regular path that still cooks markdown to HTML. Nothing in the diff indicates that `cook_method=1` would bypass cooking or cause raw markdown to be returned on edit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics migration adds force: true to an already-shipped migration, so re-execution drops top_topics with all pre-existing computed data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can cause data loss if this migration is re-run against a DB that already has `top_topics` populated (e.g., during certain reset/redo/replay scenarios).

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds migration uses force: true on a table accumulating live data, so reruns drop topic_embeds rows while topics/posts survive, causing duplicate topics to be created due to unique embed_url re-imports

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `force: true` to the new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` (`create_table :topic_embeds, force: true do |t|`), which would drop/recreate the table if the migration were rerun against a DB where `topic_embeds` already exists. That is a real, diff-grounded risk, but the finding’s framing assumes the migration will be rerun on a live DB with accumulated `topic_embeds` rows—something not shown/guaranteed by the diff (migrations normally run once and this is a new table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds migration lacks foreign keys on topic_id/post_id and no cleanup exists, so deleting a Topic/Post leaves orphaned topic_embeds rows causing crashes, 500s, or dead topic references

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` integers but no foreign keys or `dependent:` cleanup. Several code paths assume these references remain valid: `TopicEmbed.import` does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` on updates (will blow up if `post` was deleted), and `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` then `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` (can error if the topic was deleted but the embed row remains). Orphaned `topic_embeds` rows can therefore lead to exceptions/500s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration's cook_method default is a bare integer duplicating the enum mapping in Post.cook_methods as a second hand-maintained source of truth; should use default: Post.cook_methods[:regular]

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`, while the enum mapping is separately defined in `Post.cook_methods` (`Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`). This introduces a magic-number/default that must stay manually aligned with the enum, creating a maintainability risk if the enum ordering ever changes. It’s not an immediate functional defect shown by the diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded design issue (duplicated source of truth).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-40 — content_sha1 is updated unconditionally even when revise!/save fails, so failed revisions are never retried and the post update is silently lost forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb in the update branch). Since the return value of `revise!` is not checked (and `revise!` can return `false` early, and its internal `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` can fail), the SHA1 can be advanced even if the post was not actually updated, preventing future retries because subsequent imports will see matching `content_sha1` and skip the revise path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on Atom entries without a content element, and with retry: false and no per-item rescue, one malformed entry aborts the poll and drops all remaining items permanently

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil (e.g., an Atom/RSS item lacking a content element), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the whole `poll_feed` iteration. There is no per-item rescue/guard, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad entry can prevent processing of subsequent items on that run (and may keep failing on future scheduled runs if the bad entry remains).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:19-30 — the throttle SETNX key is committed before retrieval runs, so a failed retrieval consumes the 60-second throttle window and all retries silently no-op

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key via `setnx`/`expire` before `perform_retrieve` is called (`retrieve` does `perform_retrieve unless ... retrieved_recently?`). If `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` fails (network error, exception, etc.), the key still exists for 60 seconds and subsequent calls will return early. However, the code comment explicitly says "Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds" and does not condition the throttle on a successful retrieval, so this is a design/behavior concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-48 — fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username matches no user, with no log or error, leaving the embed page loading forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http, it looks up the user by SiteSetting.embed_by_username and then `return if user.blank?` with no error/log. In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it enqueues retrieval and renders `loading`, whose JS reloads every 30s. If embed_by_username is misconfigured (no matching user), retrieval will never create the TopicEmbed and the embed endpoint will keep serving the loading page indefinitely with no indication why.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-34 — Atom <id> values like urn:uuid: or tag: URIs fail the http(s) regex in TopicEmbed.import and are silently dropped with no log or error

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, each item’s URL is set to `i.link`, but if that is blank or not http(s), it falls back to `i.id` (lines 29-34). Atom `<id>` commonly uses non-http URIs like `urn:uuid:` or `tag:`; those will then be passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which immediately `return`s unless the URL matches `^https?://` (TopicEmbed.import). That means such feed items are silently skipped (no logging/error), matching the finding and resulting in dropped imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb — PollFeed#execute returns success as a no-op when settings are half-configured, reporting success while dropping work

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` is explicitly designed to be a conditional no-op unless **all** required settings are present (`feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, `embed_by_username.present?`). This behavior is reinforced by the newly added spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) that asserts it should *not* call `poll_feed` when any prerequisite is missing. The finding’s claim that it is “dropping work” or incorrectly “reporting success” isn’t verifiable from the diff—returning without polling under half-configuration appears intentional, not a defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:58 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — open(url).read calls have no read/open timeout and no body size cap, allowing worker stalls and unbounded memory/storage from remote fetches on the user-facing embed path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetching via `open(...)` without any timeout or size limits in two new code paths: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (lib open-uri) and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Both can block indefinitely and/or read arbitrarily large responses into memory, and `import_remote` is reachable from the user-facing embed flow (`EmbedController#best` → `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` → `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). This is a verifiable availability/DoS defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:4-9 — the loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no attempt cap or terminal failure state, so permanent failures are indistinguishable from slow ones

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` with a `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` inside an IIFE and no condition/counter/timeout (lines 4-9 in that new file). As written, if the background job never creates the embed/topic (e.g., network error, invalid URL, misconfiguration), the page will reload indefinitely with no terminal state, making failures look like slow loads. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/operational concern but not a strictly incorrect behavior given the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:9 — request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted JS string; a referer containing an apostrophe causes a JavaScript SyntaxError that breaks the resize postMessage and clips the iframe
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root cause: `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string without proper escaping. While it emphasizes syntax breakage from an apostrophe rather than explicitly calling out XSS, the underlying issue (unescaped header data in JS context) is the same and is what enables XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-21 — feed_key is dead code; the intended If-Modified-Since cursor throttle was never wired up, so every run fully downloads and parses the feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` a `feed_key` method is defined (lines ~20-21) but never referenced anywhere in the job; `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key` and no conditional request/cursor logic. This is diff-grounded dead code and suggests an unfinished optimization (avoid re-downloading unchanged feeds), but it’s not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — feed_polling_url is used with no http(s) URI validation and no error handling around SimpleRSS.parse, so a misconfigured setting fails silently every hour with retry: false and no admin-visible signal
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `feed_polling_url` is used without http(s) URI validation when fetching/parsing the feed, which aligns with the golden issue’s core concern: an unvalidated URL being opened/fetched. Although it emphasizes misconfiguration/silent failure and doesn’t explicitly call out SSRF/attacker control, it identifies the same underlying missing URL validation on a server-side fetch.
